question: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

In accordance with Parliament’s Rules of Procedure and the official guidelines published on Parliament’s parliamentary questions page (‘must be answered’, ‘is three weeks’), the Commission is required to reply to written questions within the following deadlines: six weeks for ordinary questions and three weeks for priority questions. However, reviewing the last 40 answers to my questions reveals a systemic failure to comply with those obligations. The average delay is currently 31 days and, in extreme cases, the delay has reached 94 days (E-001545/2024)1. Moreover, the quality of the answers given is alarming. Only 10 % of responses were fully comprehensive. The remaining 90 % were only partial replies, in which the Commission often used vague language, avoided difficult topics and, in 7 cases, completely ignored at least one of the questions asked. Given the above: 1.
What systemic or administrative problems within the Commission cause such extensive and regular delays in answering written questions?
What immediate action does the Commission intend to take to ensure that replies are provided within the deadlines set out in the Rules of Procedure?

Does the Commission have internal guidelines for formulating vague answers and ignoring specific questions posed by Members of the European Parliament? If not, how can it be forced to improve the quality of its answers?
https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2024-001545_EN.html.
